answer.evidence: This is a kei van seen from the side, not a box. Rows 6-15 form a large light-green roof band with a highlight streak. The band is bounded by a darker transition at rows 16-17 (L 153 to 125) and then the darker window band at rows 18-23. That works as a front-edge line with eave shadow, so the roof is a top surface about 10 rows tall. The south face is the body side with windows, door seams, and wheels, and it runs from about row 16 to row 41, well over 3 rows. The slanted windshield at the right adds a sloped plane.

styleAnswer.evidence: The van body is a mostly flat grey-green with a highlight band and one or two shade steps, so the main ramp has about 4 steps against 5-6 for the references. The outline is a uniform dark line around the whole silhouette and the wheels, and 88% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral. That is the sticker look, unlike the tinted dark-material outlines on the stall (1% neutral), the hedge (0%) and the well (33%). Near-flat coverage is 15%, slightly above the stall's 13% and well above the 0% of the well and hedge, and the body panels and door areas are broad flat fills with little grain or per-panel variation. At 9 visible tones per tile it only matches the hedge and is well under the stall (17) and the well (20), the closest comparisons for a large, detailed prop. The window glass has some gradient and the van is cleanly drawn, but the outline and flat panels would look shallower than the references next to them.

answer.evidence: This is a kei van facing east, drawn in side profile. Rows 16-17 form a darker edge band before the window strip in rows 18-23. Below that, the south body side runs from about row 18 to row 41 with door seams, lights and wheels, giving roughly 24 rows of front face. The roof is not a thin rim, so the van reads as three-quarter, though the roof's front edge line is weak.

That is the sticker look, not a dark tone of the adjacent material. The hedge (0% neutral) and the cheese stall (1%) use tinted edges. The side panel and roof have broad smooth areas with little grain or panel texture, and 15% of the piece is near-flat, which is above the hedge and well (0%) and similar to the stall (13%). At 9 visible tones per tile it matches the hedge but sits well below the stall (17) and well (20). Overall it is a clean but flatter, outlined piece, so it fails mainly on the outline and the shallow shading and texture.
